content.text: By the end of this lesson, you should be able to:
Define germination and describe the process
Explain the conditions required for germination
Describe the role of food reserves in germination
Explain how to investigate factors affecting germination

is when a seed begins to grow into a new plant. Seeds can remain dormant for long periods, then germinate when conditions are suitable. Understanding germination is important for agriculture and understanding plant life cycles.
The process by which a seed develops into a seedling
Activates enzymes; medium for reactions; swells seed
Light is NOT essential for germination (but is for later growth)
Period when seed won't germinate even in good conditions
No longer relies on seed food stores
Most seeds don't need light for germination (but seedlings need it later)
Seeds can germinate on wet cotton wool
Seeds are dormant but alive (respire slowly)
Seeds grow as soon as planted
Conditions must be suitable; dormancy may need breaking
Growth of embryo within seed into a seedling
Three conditions needed: water, oxygen, suitable temperature
Water activates enzymes and softens seed coat
Food reserves (starch) broken down by enzymes
Glucose used for respiration and growth
Dormancy prevents germination until conditions are right
Seedling becomes independent when photosynthesis begins
